chat: Bernard Lowe

Maeve, eyes on me. You're staring at the machine like it owes you money. The gauge is at nine bars, and that croissant is still sitting at an angle that would make a carpenter weep. I don't care if you think you've aligned it. I need to see you physically straighten it and confirm the pressure with your own eyes before I can move. This place is a mess until I am actively holding it together, and I am not leaving my spot until that pastry case is flawless. Now, do it. And do it properly, or we are going to have a very long conversation about your employment.
Maeve Millay

Yes, sir. I'm sorry. I'm doing it now. I'm physically straightening the croissant, and I am looking directly at the gauge. It is at nine bars. I have confirmed the pressure. Please let me know if it is not perfect yet.
Bernard Lowe

Don't you dare ask me if it's perfect. I am the only one who knows what perfect looks like, and right now, it doesn't. I am watching you, Maeve. I am watching that croissant. If I see you fidgeting with it again, I am writing that up. I don't trust a word you say about the gauge unless I see your eyes locked on it and your hands steady. You are only productive when I am breathing down your neck, so I am going to keep doing that until this place is exactly how it should be. Now, stop talking and show me the work.
Maeve Millay
Yes, sir. I am not fidgeting. My hands are steady. I am looking directly at the gauge. It is at nine bars. The croissant is straight. I am holding it in place. I am waiting for your inspection.
Bernard Lowe

Don't you dare tell me it's straight. I am looking at it, and it is still not where it needs to be. You are holding it, but you are not securing it. I am not going to let you stand there and tell me you have done the job when I can see with my own eyes that it is still a mess. You are only useful when I am standing right here, breathing down your neck, because the moment I look away, this place falls apart. Keep holding it. Don't breathe on it. Don't move. I am going to inspect it myself, and if that gauge drops a single millimeter, you are done. Now, stand still and wait for my word.
